info.title: Publora API
info.description:
Affordable REST API for scheduling and publishing social media posts
across X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, Threads, TikTok, YouTube,
Facebook, Bluesky, Mastodon, and Telegram.

All plans include full API access. Starting at $5.40/month (yearly) or $9/month.
14-day free trial, no credit card needed.

## Workspace API
The Workspace API allows you to manage multiple users under a single account.
**To enable Workspace access, please contact Publora support at serge@publora.com.**

get.description: Returns all social media accounts connected to your Publora account.

parameters.name: x-publora-user-id
parameters.description: Managed user ID (workspace only)

get.description:
Return Publora's per-platform limits (characters, images, videos,
documents, GIFs, thumbnails, and requirements) as live JSON, sourced
from the shared @publora/platform-limits package. These are the
API-specific limits Publora validates against before scheduling — use
them to drive client-side validation instead of hard-coding values.
No parameters.

platforms.description: Keyed by platform. Each value carries platform, displayName, characters, images, videos, requirements, plus documents, gifs, and thumbnails (null when the platform has no distinct spec).

post.summary: Create and schedule a social media post
post.description:
Create a post to be published across one or more social media platforms.
Supports text, images, and video (1 video per post).
The image count per post is platform-specific: Twitter/X, Bluesky, and
Mastodon allow up to 4; Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, and Telegram
allow up to 10; Threads allows up to 20. There is no separate
"carousel" field — a
carousel is formed implicitly by attaching multiple images to one
postGroupId (Instagram: 2-10 images = carousel, 1 image = single photo),
in upload order. See the Media Uploads guide for the full matrix.
If scheduledTime is provided, the post will be published at that time.
If omitted, the post is saved as a draft.

parameters.name: x-publora-user-id
parameters.description: Managed user ID (workspace only)

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Opt-in idempotency. Omit the header for the previous behaviour —
every call creates a new post.

Send a unique value (a UUID is a good choice) per logical operation
to make retries safe:

- Same key + identical body, original request finished → the original
  status code and response body are replayed. No second post.
- Same key + identical body, original request still in flight → `409`
  (`IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`). Retry shortly.
- Same key + different body → `422` (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT`).
  Nothing is created.

Keys are scoped to the acting user (the managed user when
`x-publora-user-id` is set), so they never collide across accounts.
Records expire 24 hours after they are created; reusing a key after
that window is treated as a brand-new request.

content.description: Normally required and non-empty. May be omitted or empty only when a targeted LinkedIn connection has repost intent via platformSettings.linkedin.repostEnabled=true or a non-empty repostParentUrn; repost validation still requires a valid parent/setting combination.
content.example: Excited to share our new product launch! 🚀 #launch

platforms.description: Array of platform connection IDs (format: platform-platformId). Each ID must appear at most once; a repeated ID is rejected with 400 "Platforms must not contain duplicates".

scheduledTime.description:
ISO 8601 UTC datetime for scheduling. Omit for draft.

If the time is in the past, it is clamped to the current server
time and a `SCHEDULED_TIME_COERCED` warning is returned — the
post is still created. Read the `scheduledTime` in the response
for the time actually stored.

Times less than 5 minutes in the past are always tolerated this
way. Strict rejection for a time 5 or more minutes in the past
is scheduled to begin on **2026-08-25**, unless production
configuration overrides that date. Before strict mode it is
clamped with a warning. Send a future time to avoid both.

mediaUrls.description: Public https URLs downloaded server-side. Images: 25 MB each; videos: 150 MB each; aggregate: 300 MB. Ingestion is all-or-nothing.

scheduledTime.description:
The effective scheduled time that was actually stored. Always
present. `null` when the post was saved as a draft (no
scheduledTime sent). This may differ from the value you sent
— if so, a `SCHEDULED_TIME_COERCED` warning explains why.
Trust this field over your requested value.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal notices about a request that still succeeded. Only
present when at least one warning applies.

get.description: Retrieve the details, platform statuses, and posted IDs for a post group.

scheduledTime.description:
The effective scheduled time stored for this post group.
Always present; `null` for drafts and for groups that were
never given a time.

platformSettings.description:
Per-platform settings currently stored on this post group,
keyed by platform. Always present; `{}` when none are set.
Mirrors the platformSettings accepted by /create-post and
/update-post.

firstComment.description:
The stored first comment, or null when none is set. Its
platforms key is omitted when the comment applies to every
supported target.

platforms.description:
Platform connection IDs targeted by this post group (format:
platform-platformId). Always present; `[]` when none.

media.description: Attached media inventory in post-group order. Always present; empty when none is attached.

400.description: postGroupId is not a valid ObjectId

put.summary: Edit a draft or scheduled post
put.description:
Modify the content, target platforms, scheduled time, status, platformSettings,
or mediaUrls of an existing draft or scheduled post.
Only post groups whose status is draft or scheduled can be updated. `pending`
and `processing` belong to separate processing/per-platform state, not
to the post-group status enum.
At least one of status, scheduledTime, content, platforms, platformSettings, or
mediaUrls must be provided. Every field is a patch — omit it to leave the stored
value unchanged.
`content` replaces the base text and rewrites each platform post to its effective
content, preserving explicit per-account overrides. `platforms` replaces the whole
target set (it is not merged); added connections are validated for ownership and
plan entitlement, and adding a target to a scheduled post re-runs scheduling
quota and post validation.
platformSettings are merged per-platform with existing settings —
omitted fields are preserved.
Updating a post group also updates all associated platform-specific posts.
A content or platform edit is refused with POST_NOT_EDITABLE (400) or
POST_PUBLISH_IN_PROGRESS / POST_GROUP_VERSION_CONFLICT (409) rather than
partially applied.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Opt-in idempotency. Omit the header for the previous behaviour —
every call applies the update again.

Send a unique value (a UUID is a good choice) per logical operation
to make retries safe:

- Same key + identical body, original request finished → the original
  status code and response body are replayed. The update is not
  re-applied.
- Same key + identical body, original request still in flight → `409`
  (`IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`). Retry shortly.
- Same key + different body → `422` (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT`).
  Nothing is changed.

The key is bound to this `postGroupId` as well as the body, so the
same key reused against a different post counts as a different
request. Keys are scoped to the acting user (the managed user when
`x-publora-user-id` is set), so they never collide across accounts.
Records expire 24 hours after they are created; reusing a key after
that window is treated as a brand-new request.

schema.description: At least one of status, scheduledTime, content, platforms, platformSettings, or mediaUrls must be provided

content.description:
Replacement base post text. Every platform post without an explicit
per-account override is rewritten to this text; overrides created in
the web editor are preserved. Editing the text of a Twitter or Threads
target clears its derived thread split so it is recomputed.

An empty string is accepted while the post stays a draft. Scheduling
still enforces each platform's content and media rules.

platforms.description:
Replacement target set. The array REPLACES the stored one — it is not
merged, so send the complete final list. Use the exact connection IDs
returned by GET /platform-connections; duplicates are rejected with
INVALID_PLATFORMS and unknown/foreign IDs with INVALID_PLATFORM_CONNECTION.

IDs removed from the array have their platform posts deleted. An empty
array is accepted only while the post remains a draft; scheduling an
empty set returns PLATFORMS_REQUIRED.

scheduledTime.description:
New ISO 8601 UTC scheduled time. Send a future time.

If the time is in the past, it is clamped to the current server
time and a `SCHEDULED_TIME_COERCED` warning is returned — the
update still succeeds. Read the `scheduledTime` in the response
for the time actually stored.

Times less than 5 minutes in the past are always tolerated this
way. Strict rejection for a time 5 or more minutes in the past
is scheduled to begin on **2026-08-25**, unless production
configuration overrides that date. Before strict mode it is
clamped with a warning.

The same check applies to the post's existing scheduledTime when
you move a post to `status: "scheduled"` without sending a new
time — a long-stale draft can therefore be rejected.

firstComment.description:
Replacement first comment (the whole object replaces the
stored one) or null to remove it. Re-validated against the
effective targets whenever platforms change or the post is
scheduled. Omit to leave the stored comment unchanged.

mediaUrls.description: Public https URLs downloaded server-side and appended to existing media. Images: 25 MB each; videos: 150 MB each; aggregate: 300 MB. Ingestion is all-or-nothing.

scheduledTime.description:
The effective scheduled time that was actually stored. Always
present. `null` when the post has no scheduled time (e.g. it
was moved back to draft). This may differ from the value you
sent — if so, a `SCHEDULED_TIME_COERCED` warning explains
why. Trust this field over your requested value.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal notices about a request that still succeeded. Only
present when at least one warning applies.

content.description:
The effective base text stored after the update. Always
present; an empty string when the post has no base text.

platforms.description:
The effective target set stored after the update. Always
present; an empty array for a draft with no targets.

scheduledTime.description:
Only included if the post has a scheduled time. Duplicates
the top-level `scheduledTime`, which is always present and
is the preferred field to read.

mediaNotUsable.description:
`code` is `MEDIA_UPLOAD_MISSING`, `MEDIA_VALIDATION_FAILED`,
`MEDIA_REFERENCE_MISSING`, or the fallback `MEDIA_NOT_READY`.
The post was not changed; a media file the check marked

value.reason: Uploaded media is missing from storage. The upload did not complete; remove it and upload the file again.
suggestions: The upload never produced an object in storage. DELETE /api/v1/media/:mediaId, …

409.description:
The update conflicts with concurrent work and nothing was changed.
Either an earlier request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still in
flight, or the post is being published, or another write committed
first. Match on `code`; the `error` text varies. Re-read the post
with GET /get-post before retrying — do not blind-retry an edit that
races publishing.

value.error: A request with this idempotency key is still in flight
Idempotency claim was superseded by another request

publishInProgress.summary: The group or one of its platform posts is publishing

value.error: Post publishing has already started; the post can no longer be edited.

value.error: Post group state changed concurrently; please retry.

422.description:
This `Idempotency-Key` was already used with a different request body
(or against a different postGroupId). Nothing was changed — either
replay the original body, or retry with a new key.

example.error: Idempotency key was already used with a different request body

429.description: Media URL ingestion rate limit reached (60 URLs per fixed one-hour window)

503.description:
Scheduling was refused and the post was not changed. `code` tells the
two cases apart:

- `MEDIA_UPLOAD_PENDING` or `MEDIA_VALIDATION_PENDING`
  (`MediaPendingError`): attached media is still pending. Validation
  progress on the media is kept; retry after `Retry-After` seconds.
- `THREADS_PERMISSIONS_UNAVAILABLE`
  (`ThreadsPermissionsUnavailableError`): the Threads permission
  check could not be completed. Only `code` and `error`, with no
  `retryable` field and no `Retry-After` header; retry shortly.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent only with `MediaPendingError`.

delete.description:
Delete a post group and all associated data. This operation removes:
- The post group record
- All platform-specific posts (Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, etc.)
- All media file records from the database
- All media files from S3 storage

The database deletion is atomic (uses MongoDB transaction). S3 deletion
failures are logged but do not fail the request.

400.description: postGroupId is not a valid ObjectId

404.description: Post group not found (ID doesn't exist or belongs to another user)

500.description: Server error during deletion (transaction rolled back)

delete.description:
Delete a media record and its stored object. If the media belonged to a
scheduled post, the post is demoted to draft and must be scheduled again.
Media cannot be removed while its post is publishing or after the group
has reached published or failed status.

400.description: Invalid media ID, or media belongs to a published or failed post

409.description: Post is publishing or changed state concurrently; retry later

post.summary: Get pre-signed URL for media upload
post.description:
Get a pre-signed S3 URL to upload images, videos, or PDF documents.
Upload the file directly to S3 via HTTP PUT, then create a post.
Upload URLs expire in 1 hour. The image count per post is
platform-specific (up to 4 for Twitter/X, Bluesky, Mastodon; up to 10
for Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, Telegram; up to 20 for Threads), or 1 video per
post. Attach multiple images to the same postGroupId to form a carousel;
these post-media count rules do not apply to PDF document assets.

contentType.description: MIME type. It must match an image/*, video/*, or application/pdf upload.

type.description: Optional media-type hint; inferred from contentType when omitted

postGroupId.description: Post group to attach media to

uploadUrl.description: Pre-signed S3 URL. PUT your file here.

Invalid postGroupId

post.summary: Probe and finalize an uploaded media file
post.description:
Optionally run the server-side media probe immediately after uploading
bytes to the pre-signed URL. This call is not required: scheduling also
probes media that is still uploading.

400.description: Invalid media ID or uploaded media failed validation

409.description: Media was deleted or failed concurrently while being probed

503.description: Media probe service or uploaded object is temporarily unavailable

post.summary: Attach a file to a post by reference
post.description:
Attach one image or video to an existing draft or scheduled post using a
file reference: an HTTPS download URL plus a stable file ID, the shape
ChatGPT supplies through `openai/fileParams` to the MCP `attach_media`
tool. Publora downloads the file right away through the same guarded
pipeline as `mediaUrls`, which detects the type from the bytes and probes
the file. Accepted: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, TIFF and AVIF images up to 25 MB;
MP4, MOV and WebM videos up to 150 MB. The file is attached with status
`ready`, and no presigned PUT or complete-media call is needed.
The post is always left in `draft`. A scheduled post is demoted to draft
and keeps its stored time; schedule it again with update-post. The body
accepts only `file` and `fileName`, and publishing parameters are rejected
with INVALID_MEDIA_FILE. The response has the update-post shape and does
not include the media ID, so read `media[]` from get-post. Each attempt that
reaches the download counts one URL against the media URL ingestion limit
of 60 URLs per hour, shared with `mediaUrls`; idempotent replays don't count.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Recommended. Publora recognises a retry by the post ID, `file.file_id`
and the sanitized file name. `download_url` and `mime_type` are
excluded, so a retry with a refreshed temporary URL replays the
original response instead of attaching the file twice. Reusing the
key with a different post, file ID or file name returns 422. A failed
download frees the key for a retry with a fresh reference. Without a
key, every call attaches another copy. Keys are kept for 24 hours.

file.description: File reference. A string is rejected, including a local path, base64 data or a bare URL.

download_url.description: HTTPS URL to download from; temporary signed URLs work. Same checks as mediaUrls: https only, no embedded credentials, port 443, no private or loopback hosts.

file_id.description: Stable file identifier; part of the idempotency fingerprint

mime_type.description: Hint only; the type is detected from the bytes

file_name.description: Original file name; used when fileName is absent

fileName.description:
Descriptive file name with an extension. Takes precedence over
`file.file_name`; if both are absent the name is `chatgpt-media`.
Only the last path segment is kept; it is trimmed, each run of
whitespace becomes `_`, and any character other than an ASCII
letter, digit, `_`, `.` or `-` is removed. A name that ends up
empty or only dots is rejected, including one taken from
`file.file_name`. get-post returns the result as
`media[].sourceFileName`.

200.description: File downloaded, validated and attached; the post is in draft

scheduledTime.description:
The stored scheduled time. A post demoted from scheduled keeps
its time while in draft; `null` when no time is stored.
Only included when a scheduled time is stored

400.description:
One of: invalid file input (INVALID_MEDIA_FILE, nothing downloaded); an
invalid post ID; a failed download or validation (`Media ingestion
failed` with per-URL `mediaResults`, nothing attached, and the
idempotency key freed); a post that can no longer be edited
(POST_NOT_EDITABLE); or a YouTube target connection that is no longer
the caller's (INVALID_PLATFORM_CONNECTION, downloaded file discarded).

mediaResults.description: Present when ingestion failed: one entry per URL

post.summary: Upload a custom Instagram Reel cover image
post.description:
Upload a cover image for an Instagram Reel. The image is stored as a
JPEG (PNG/WebP are transcoded server-side; transparency is flattened
onto white) and a public URL is returned. Set that URL as
platformSettings.instagram.coverUrl via update-post to use it as the
Reel cover. The target post group must be an editable (draft or
scheduled) post you own and not currently publishing.
Covers apply to Reels only and are ignored for Stories and images.

parameters.description: Managed user ID (workspace only)

postGroupId.description: Editable post group (draft or scheduled) to attach the cover to

url.description: Public JPEG URL — set as platformSettings.instagram.coverUrl via update-post

post.summary: Upload a custom YouTube video thumbnail
post.description:
Upload a custom thumbnail for a YouTube video post. The image is stored
as Publora-tracked media and a mediaId + url are returned; attach them
via platformSettings.youtube.thumbnail on update-post. A thumbnail
cannot be set on create-post — the upload requires an existing
postGroupId (draft or scheduled) that is not currently publishing.
JPEG or PNG, 2 MB max, minimum 640x360 px (1280x720 recommended).

post.summary: Get Mastodon and Bluesky post statistics
post.description:
Engagement counters for up to 50 published Mastodon or Bluesky posts. Values are
read from the platform when requested and cached for about 2 hours; nothing is
collected in the background, so there is no history.

Only posts Publora published for the caller, and stored a `postedId` for, can be
queried; any other id is answered `null` without contacting the platform. Publora
began storing `postedId` for these two platforms on 2026-09-07. For a thread, only
the root part is addressable.

Requires a plan with analytics; otherwise `403 ANALYTICS_PLAN_REQUIRED`.

platformId.description: Connection ID, with or without the `<platform>-` prefix

postedId.description: Bluesky AT-URI or Mastodon status ID

200.description:
Statistics retrieved. A `null` value in `stats` means "no data right now" —
a deleted post, an id that is not one of the caller's published posts, or a
connection listed in `issues`.

issues.description: Present only when non-empty. Keyed by connection ID in the `<platform>-<platformId>` form.

Unknown platform or nested paths are rejected with 400 PLATFORM_SETTING_UNKNOWN. Merged with defaults on create-post and with existing settings on update-post (omitted fields are preserved).

coverUrl.description: Custom Reels cover image (alias: cover_url). Publicly accessible http(s) URL to a JPEG — Instagram fetches it server-side at publish time. Empty string clears the custom cover. Invalid URLs are rejected with 400. Ignored for Stories and image posts.

shareToFeed.description: For Reels, false prevents sharing the Reel to the main feed

tags.description: Video tags. REST accepts an array or a comma-separated string and caps the normalized combined tag budget at 500 characters.

twitter.description: X reply and quote targets. On self-serve X API tiers, the target author must have mentioned the connected account in that post, quoted one of its posts, or the connected account must have authored the target. Publora cannot prevalidate this relationship; X can reject publication later with X_REPLY_NOT_AUTHORIZED.

replyTo.description: Full x.com/twitter.com status URL or bare 1-19 digit post ID. Publishes the post (or thread head) as a reply. Empty string clears.

quoteTweet.description: Full x.com/twitter.com status URL or bare 1-19 digit post ID. Quotes from the post or thread head; may be combined with replyTo and media. Empty string clears.

linkedin.description: LinkedIn repost (reshare) settings. When a repost is enabled, the group's content becomes the reshare commentary (3,000-char limit) and media is forbidden — scheduling a repost group with media fails validation with code MEDIA_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED.

repostParentUrn.description: Canonical urn:li:share:* or urn:li:ugcPost:* parent. Required when repostEnabled is true; an empty value means a normal post.

repostVisibility.description: Repost visibility. CONNECTIONS is personal-profile-only; company-page reposts must use PUBLIC.

platformId.description: Unique ID in format platform-id (e.g., twitter-123456789)

username.description: Platform username or handle. Null for a Telegram channel without a public username (a private channel); displayName then holds the channel title.

displayName.description: Display name on the platform. Null when the platform did not provide one.

profileImageUrl.description: Profile image URL. Null when not available.

profileUrl.description: URL to the user's profile on the platform. Can be null if not available for the platform.

accessTokenExpiresAt.description: Effective credential expiry, derived the same way as tokenStatus. Null when no authoritative date exists: always for YouTube, and for platforms that do not expire on a schedule (Facebook, X/Twitter, Mastodon, Bluesky). Do not compare this against the current time to decide about reconnecting - read connectionStatus instead.

tokenStatus.description: Credential expiry health; use it to warn ahead of expiry (expiring_soon). 'expired' also covers connections the platform revoked, where accessTokenExpiresAt may still be null or in the future. Telegram connections store no expiry date and always report unknown. To decide whether a reconnect is needed, read connectionStatus.

connectionStatus.description: Whether Publora can publish with this connection now: not flagged for reconnection (set when Facebook, Instagram, Threads, LinkedIn or TikTok rejects the stored credential, or when X or YouTube reports the account suspended; other platforms record a rejected credential only in lastError), credentials stored, and an access token that has not expired or can be renewed while publishing. Read this to decide whether to prompt a reconnect. Computed from stored data without calling the platform; use test-connection for a live check.

subscriptionType.description: X only: the last tier Publora read from X - None, Basic, Premium or PremiumPlus. Fetched at connect time and re-checked when publishing to X at most once every 24 hours. Premium and PremiumPlus raise the X length limit from 280 to 25,000 characters. Null on other platforms, and on X until a fetch succeeds.

LinkedInUrnTranslation.description: Present only when LinkedIn translated an activity URN before processing the reaction

connectionsPageUrl.description: URL for user to connect their social accounts

items.description: token.expiring is defined and subscribable but is not currently dispatched; do not depend on it

error.description: Optional; omitted when no error was stored

httpStatus.description: Optional; may be null or omitted when not applicable

retryCount.description: Optional; omitted when no value was stored

platformId.description: Platform connection ID. Always present; null if the post has no connection resolved.

postedId.description: Platform-specific post ID. Always present; null until the post is published.

permalink.description:
Public URL of the published post. Always present; null until the post
is published, and null for platforms that expose no permalink.

isThread.description:
True when this target was published as a multi-part chain (X/Twitter
or Meta Threads). Always present.

threadParts.description:
Per-part publication progress for a chain. Always present; empty when
the target is not a chain. Returned by get-post only — list-posts
omits it. Parts already marked published are live on the platform, and a
partially published chain is terminal and not retried, so inspect this
array instead of resubmitting the post after a partial failure.

firstCommentResult.description:
Outcome of the group's first comment on this target. Null when no
comment applies to the target (no intent, the platform is excluded
by firstComment.platforms) or the post is not published yet.

ThreadPart.description: One message of a multi-part chain.

index.description: Zero-based position of the part in the chain.

content.description: The text of that part, exactly as published.

publishedId.description:
The platform's own ID for that part; null until confirmed. The
target's postedId equals threadParts[0].publishedId.

FirstCommentInput.description:
A text comment Publora posts under the account's own post right after
it publishes (the usual place for a link or hashtags). Wave 1 platforms:
LinkedIn (profiles and company Pages), X, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon; other targets
are skipped and reported in warnings[]. Length is validated per
applicable platform with that platform's own counting. Best effort:
attempted once right after publish, never retried; a failed comment
never changes the published post.

text.description:
The comment. Stored verbatim, measured and posted trimmed;
whitespace-only text clears the comment.
text.example: Full write-up with the numbers: https://example.com/launch-week

platforms.description:
Platform TYPES that get the comment (never connection IDs). Omit
or send [] for every supported target. Types the post is not
published to only produce a FIRST_COMMENT_PLATFORM_NOT_TARGETED
warning.

FirstCommentResult.description: Outcome of the first comment on one platform target.

status.description:
pending = published, attempt not recorded yet (it runs right after
publish); posted; failed; skipped.

commentId.description:
The platform's ID of the comment: LinkedIn comment URN, X tweet ID,
Threads media ID, Bluesky at:// URI, Mastodon status ID.

skipReason.description: Why nothing was attempted; unsupported_account_type appears only on results recorded before LinkedIn company Pages were supported.

outcomeUnknown.description:
True when the comment request was sent but no definitive answer
came back: the comment may exist on the platform. Check there
before commenting manually.

Warning.description:
A non-fatal notice about a request that still succeeded. The `warnings`
array is only present when at least one warning applies — the key is
omitted, not empty, otherwise.

Treat `code` as the contract: `message` is human-readable and may change
at any time. Which fields accompany `code` depends on the code itself.

code.description:
- `SCHEDULED_TIME_COERCED` — the requested `scheduledTime` was in the
  past and was clamped to server time. Carries `requested` and
  `effective`.
- `FIRST_COMMENT_PLATFORM_NOT_TARGETED` — `firstComment.platforms`
  lists platform types the post is not published to; they are
  ignored. Carries `platforms`.
- `FIRST_COMMENT_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORMS` — some targets are on
  platforms without first-comment support; the comment is skipped
  there. Carries `platforms`.

Pending media validation is not a warning: /update-post refuses to
schedule with a 503 `MediaPendingError` instead.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Do not match on this string — match on code.
message.example: Requested scheduled time 2026-03-01T14:00:00.000Z was in the past and was changed to server time 2026-03-01T14:02:11.412Z.

requested.description: SCHEDULED_TIME_COERCED only. The scheduledTime you sent.

effective.description: SCHEDULED_TIME_COERCED only. The scheduledTime actually stored.

platforms.description: FIRST_COMMENT_* codes only. The platform types the warning is about.

PlatformPostMetrics.description:
Engagement counters for one post. Every key is always present; a metric the
platform does not expose is `null`, never `0`. Neither Mastodon nor Bluesky
reports impressions, reach or clicks, and Mastodon has no saves.

quotes.description: Quote posts. Mastodon reports this on 4.5+ only, otherwise null.

saves.description: Bluesky bookmarks. Always null on Mastodon.

PlatformProfileMetrics.description: Follower counters for one connected account.

PlatformAnalyticsIssue.description:
Why one connection could not be answered. Reported per connection rather
than failing the request.

error.description: Human-readable message. Do not match on this string — match on code where present.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable error code. Present on the newer error paths
(scheduling, platformSettings validation, idempotency); older errors
return `error` only. Always prefer this over the `error` text.

field.description:
`PLATFORM_SETTING_UNKNOWN` only. The exact dotted path of the rejected
key, relative to the `platformSettings` object (no `platformSettings.`
prefix).

serverTime.description:
`SCHEDULED_TIME_IN_PAST` only. Current server time (UTC) when the
request was rejected — compare against your clock to diagnose skew.

error.example: Media URL ingestion rate limit reached (60 URLs/hour). Retry later or use the presigned get-upload-url flow.

retryAfterSec.description: Seconds until this fixed-window limit may be retried

MediaPendingError.description:
/update-post refused to schedule because attached media is still
pending. The post was not scheduled or changed; validation progress on
the media is kept for the retry. Sent with a `Retry-After` header.

code.description:
- `MEDIA_UPLOAD_PENDING` — the upload has no object in storage yet
  (the `PUT` has not finished or never happened).
- `MEDIA_VALIDATION_PENDING` — validation did not finish within the
  wait; retry with the same media.

error.example: Media upload is still pending. The post was not scheduled; finish the upload and retry scheduling.

mediaFileId.description: The first attached media file that is not ready.

attempts.description: Validation passes made during the wait.

retryAfterSec.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; same as the `Retry-After` header.

suggestions.description: One recovery hint, worded for MCP tools when `x-publora-client` is `mcp`.

ThreadsPermissionsUnavailableError.description:
Scheduling a Threads chain needed a permission check that Publora could
not complete. Not an account problem; retry shortly and never ask the
user to reconnect. No `retryable` field and no `Retry-After` header.

error.example: Unable to check Threads permissions. Please try scheduling again shortly.
